items.headline: Colorado counties begin paying CCCAP providers on enrollment, not daily attendance, in August 2026
items.summary: Removes absence-driven revenue leakage — subsidy revenue becomes predictable for Colorado centers starting this month.

items.headline: CDEC adopts new CCCAP rules: financial safeguards plus processes to clear waitlists and lift freezes
items.summary: Creates a path to re-open enrollment where freezes had capped subsidized demand.

items.headline: Nearly 14,000 Colorado children on CCCAP waitlists or under enrollment freezes
items.summary: Subsidy rationing suppresses reachable demand in Colorado markets until freezes actually lift.

items.headline: Utah HB 190 raises employer child care tax credit from 10% to 30% for small businesses
items.summary: Employer-sponsored demand becomes materially cheaper in Utah — a corporate-partnership angle for SLC centers.

items.headline: Utah HB 453 early childhood funding account rejected on the floor; no state ECE funding
items.summary: Utah still provides no recurring state early-childhood funding, leaving SLC economics fully private-pay dependent.
